parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is mostly cohesive. Order, OrderLine, OrderStatus, Product, the repository ports, DomainError and StockAllocationService all belong to one order/stock domain, and status-transition rules live only in order-status.ts (nextFulfilmentStatus, isCancellable), which Order uses. But the insufficient-stock invariant is written twice. Product.reserve guards `quantity > this.available` and throws DomainError("INSUFFICIENT_STOCK", "Insufficient stock for product ..."). StockAllocationService.reserve repeats the same comparison against product.availableQuantity with the same error code and the same message template, so it can check every line before changing any stock. The rule now lives in two places and can drift. A query on Product (e.g. canReserve) would keep it in one place and still allow the all-or-nothing check. This matches the rubric's fail condition for duplicated invariants.

violations.message: StockAllocationService.reserve repeats Product.reserve's insufficient-stock check: the same `quantity > available` comparison, the same INSUFFICIENT_STOCK code and the same message template. The rule now lives in both Product and the service; Product should expose a single check (e.g. canReserve) for the service to call.
